analysis.title: Back to square 1 in beta rotation, where next?
key_insights: Beta rotation has round-tripped. Eurozone Banks vs Staples is back to its May-June starting point, flat on the year. Eurozone Banks are up 11% ytd versus 17% for Staples, after being up 22% vs down 3% by late September.

From June to September, bond yields spiked and Defensives, Low Vol and bond proxies were sold. Beta reversed from end September, coinciding with the peak in bond yields. JPM says the summer's crowded trades have had a clear out.

Over the last month, Stoxx 600 Healthcare and Food, Beverage and Tobacco rose 16-17% while Banks fell 3%, Metals & Mining fell 9% and Technology fell 9%. European Semis lost 25%. In the US, Staples and Healthcare are up double digits and Technology is down 17%.

JPM expects any renewed Iran-related escalation to be short lived, and says to use dips to add, as it has advised since the second half of March. Brent is back below $100 on Iran talk headlines after flirting with $120 at the end of October.
Markets have tended to be choppy into midterms and much stronger afterwards. JPM calls last week's move an anomaly and a more attractive entry point.

SOX fell 12% in one day on 5 Nov 2026. Falls of this size cluster around recessions or sharp positioning shocks that did not become recessions. JPM expects the non-recession path (quick recovery) because activity indicators are constructive and Semis earnings are rising.

The S&P500 fell more than 4% on 5 Nov 2026. Outside recessions, such drops have been followed by an average 10% gain over 3 months, positive 100% of the time (median +3% at 1w, +4% at 1m, +10% at 3m).

JPM reiterates its early-October call that bond yields have peaked. The US 10Y crossed 5% in late September for the first time in two decades and peaked near 5.3%. It has since fallen close to 50bp. JPM reads this as a policy repricing, not a loss of fiscal or inflation credibility.

Hikes priced by year end fell from 39bp to around 19bp and term premia has stopped rising. JPM economists expect one final 25bp Fed hike in December, then a hold. JPM forecasts the US 10Y at 5.05% in Dec 26.

Headline inflation is higher but core is stable. US core run rate is about 0.2pp above its pre-war pace, which JPM calls an energy shock and not broad-based inflation. 5Y-5Y inflation forwards edged lower even as Brent neared $120.

AI capex funding fears do not worry JPM. Hyperscaler FCF is set to swing from $233bn in 2024 to minus $145bn in 2027, but the Cross Asset team estimates $260bn of extra high grade supply would add only 5-10bp to yields.

Cyclicals have lagged Defensives since early October (Europe about 15%, US about 10%). JPM reads the gap with yields as a growth scare, not a 2022-style unwind, since inflation is contained and central banks are not behind the curve. It expects the gap to close via a Cyclical rebound.

Hyperscalers have de-rated to almost one standard deviation cheap, at 10-year lows (cheapest since 2012 per the key calls page). In Jun/Jul the Kospi fell 40% and SOX about 30% while the S&P 500 slipped only 0.5%. Last week's sell-off was panic-driven and hit the broader market.

Growth indicators are resilient. Global composite PMI is 53.2 (53.7 in another table), US ISM is near a four-year high, Eurozone manufacturing PMI is at its highest since May 2022, and IFO made a four-year high. JPM sees a mid-cycle, not late-cycle, economy.

Taiwan export orders, JPM's leading indicator for earnings, are still rising and have not peaked. Consensus 2026e EPS growth is 30.3% MSCI World, 34.3% US, 24.1% Eurozone. 2027e is 15.4% World, 18.3% US, 12.1% Eurozone.

JPM stays with its broadening call (Tech will not be the only story) but does not see AI as an outright sell. Semis remain its preferred AI exposure. Key AI stocks are down from peak: SK Hynix -61%, Samsung -48%, MU -44%, AVGO -39%, AMD -33%, ASML -26%, NVDA -21%, TSMC -17%. The S&P500 momentum factor lost all its ytd gains, down more than 40% from mid-June highs.

Ytd P/E derating is 10% for MSCI World (table shows 12.8%). US 12m fwd P/E fell from 21.7 to 18.1, EM -27%, Eurozone -5%. JPM says investors should add to equities into year end if the drivers show traction.

Allocation: Overweight equities (65% vs 60% benchmark), underweight cash, neutral bonds. Overweight EM and Eurozone, underweight DM, neutral US, Japan and UK. Sector overweights are Metals & Mining, Capital Goods, Semis, Construction Materials, Consumer Durables. Underweights are Energy, Staples, Media, Software, Insurance.

JPM sees potential for geopolitical re-escalation after midterms, with a fresh oil spike, as a possible 'escalate in order to de-escalate' template. It has turned more positive on Defense (favouring modernization plays) after being cautious since summer 2025.
Dec 26 index targets: MSCI Eurozone 420 (+12% vs 376), Euro Stoxx 50 6,800 (+11% vs 6,145), MSCI Europe 2,750 (+8%), STOXX 600 680 (+5%), FTSE 100 11,000 (+3%).

risk_factors: Renewed Iran escalation after midterms and a fresh oil spike.
A growth scare turning into contraction if ISM and PMIs fall below 50.
Inflation fears worsening, with a Fed hike and rising yields (the downside scenario).
AI complex leverage and weaker hyperscaler FCF (minus $145bn in 2027), and AI commoditization risk.
Valuation: US forward P/E near 19x is still stretched versus real yields.
SOX falls of this size also cluster around recessions (2000-02, 2008).
Households' equity weight is at a record high.
charts_described: Table 1 lists SOX forward returns after its largest one-day falls. Average +4% at 1 month, +7% at 3 months, +11% at 6 months, with the 5 Nov 2026 fall of -12% shown with no forward data.
Table 9 shows peak-to-current moves in key AI stocks: SK Hynix -61%, Samsung -48%, MU -44%, AVGO -39%, AMD -33%, ASML -26%, NVDA -21%, TSMC -17%.
Figure 3 lists Stoxx 600 sector performance over the last month, with Basic Resources at -9.2% and Healthcare around +16-17%.
vol_and_positioning: Overall equity positioning is rather light, and technicals in crowded areas have improved. Households' equity weight as a share of total assets is at a record high.
SOX fell 12% in a single day on 5 Nov 2026, with S&P500 falling more than 4% the same day. JPM says falls of this size are rare.
S&P500 momentum factor long-short has lost all its ytd gains, down more than 40% from mid-June highs. On 14 Sept Software beat Semis by 12.2% in a day, the largest move in the series.
Investor sentiment is described as extremely fragile.
S&P 500 is 3% below all-time highs and SXXP 2% below, while risk-off is more visible beneath the surface.
EPFR flows to 28 Oct: US equity funds took in $14.9bn in 1 week and $63.9bn in 1 month, UK funds had outflows of $1.0bn in the week.
geopolitical: Iran conflict: Brent is back below $100 on positive headlines around Iran talks, but JPM does not rule out fresh escalation after midterms.
JPM expects any re-escalation to be short lived since the war is unpopular, and treats it as a dip to buy, as since March.
US midterm election results are read as adding to the view that the conflict will not be prolonged.
Possible 'escalate in order to de-escalate' pattern in oil.

tension_points.bull_case: Yields peaked for the right reasons: policy repricing, stable inflation expectations, and less AI crowding out. JPM expects the market to read this as good news and beta to rebound.
tension_points.bear_case: The peak could reflect concern over where the economy is in the cycle, with cyclicals underperforming and a growth scare spreading.
tension_points.what_invalidates: ISM and PMIs falling below 50, or inflation fears worsening with the Fed hiking more.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers have de-rated to 10-year lows, Semis earnings keep rising, and non-recession SOX falls have typically recovered quickly.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher leverage and weaker FCF justify part of the repricing, and SOX falls of this size also cluster around recessions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A recession, with activity indicators and ISM/PMIs dropping below 50.

tension_points.bull_case: Any re-escalation should be short lived, and has been a dip to buy since March.
tension_points.bear_case: A fresh oil spike and bout of market weakness after midterms.
